issues.title: Setting one agent's model changed another agent's model
issues.description:
Our troupe.yml shares settings between agents with a YAML anchor:

    defaults: &d
      model: opus
    coder:
      settings: *d
    reviewer:
      settings: *d

I ran `troupe config set coder.settings.model sonnet` and now `reviewer` uses sonnet too, and `defaults`
changed. I only meant to change coder.

Expected: changing `defaults.model` changes everyone (that's what the anchor is for). Changing
`coder.settings.model` should not silently change anyone else — refuse, and let me explicitly ask for coder's
copy to be expanded so I can override it.
issues.close_reason: Fixed on main (9a638fb, mission troupe-config-anchor-aliases-01M48SQ8, step 6 Aliases). set through an alias now exits 3 naming the alias and --expand-alias, changing nothing; set at the anchor changes every alias; set --expand-alias gives the path its own block-style copy marked '# expanded from *d by troupe'. Verified on main with the reporter's file; full suite 2135 passed, mypy --strict and ruff clean.

issues.title: --in-include refused (exit 3) for chained mapping-form includes

Out of spec; conservative fix: refuse with WriteRefused naming PATH and file. Planned for WP04/WP05 of troupe-config-include-overrides-01M46FY4.
issues.close_reason: Not reachable via CLI: loader rejects anchors/tags with exit 4 (step 1). WP04 added a defensive WriteRefused backstop in convert_include_edits (_refuse_properties) with direct tests; recorded as an edge case in spec.

issues.title: watch: a failing remote include holds the theatre lock up to 10 s per retry
issues.description: Post-merge review R-b (troupe-config-remote-includes-01M4BMJ5): while unloadable, watch retries every tick (S-6, step-3 rule); each retry fetches the failing URL inside open_session under the theatre lock, bounded by the 10 s deadline, so other commands can stall. Consider backing off retries after a FetchError or fetching outside the lock.

issues.title: Remote includes: no size limit on fetched bodies (product decision)
issues.description: Adversarial finding A-1 (research.md, troupe-config-remote-includes-01M4BMJ5): remote.fetch reads the whole body into memory with no cap, so a hostile or broken server can exhaust memory. The spec sets no limit and inventing one would be a new requirement (TROUPE-008), so this needs a product-owner decision: cap (and exit 4 naming the URL) or document.
issues.close_reason: Chose a 1 MiB body limit (spec S-14): larger bodies are a failed fetch, exit 4. Merged to main.

issues.title: remote.fetch: create the socket inside the per-address try (IPv6-disabled hosts)
issues.description: In src/troupe/remote.py _connect, socket creation happens outside the per-address try; stdlib create_connection creates it inside, so an address family the kernel cannot create (e.g. IPv6 disabled while DNS returns AAAA first) fails the whole fetch instead of trying the next address. Found in WP01 cycle-2 review (troupe-config-remote-includes-01M4BMJ5); non-blocking. Fix: move socket() into the try and add a test with a patched getaddrinfo returning an unsupported family first.

issues.title: Verifier: compare which side (base/override) each merged key comes from
issues.description: WP04 review cycle 1 (non-blocking): apply._same_outside compares MergedMapping vs MergedMapping only by ref target and merged entries; a value moving between override and base side with an identical merged result would pass verification. Placement prevents it today. Consider also comparing the side each key comes from. Mission troupe-config-include-overrides-01M46FY4.

issues.title: Verifier: merged-vs-merged comparison doesn't detect a value moving between include and override
issues.description: Verifier hardening (non-blocking, found in WP04/WP05 reviews): apply._same_outside compares merged views by ref target + merged entries + allowed key orders only. (1) Off the route, a value moving between the included file and an override with identical merged result is not detected. (2) On the route, the verifier does not check that the new key landed in the file placement chose: crafted writes of the new key at the end of an intermediate include (c.yaml) or the root override are accepted. Placement prevents both today (no CLI repro). Fix: verify the written file/mapping of the added key equals the placement target, and compare base/override sides off the route.

issues.title: Lineage tests: small hardening follow-ups from WP05 review
issues.description: Non-blocking findings from the WP05 review (mission troupe-config-lineage-01M436R0): (1) move the pwd.getpwuid patch justification in test_lineage_cli US1-5 into the test docstring; (2) US2-3 watch test should also assert both watch change ids differ from the import change id; (3) the no-login-variables test computes expected via pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()) and would itself fail in a container without a passwd entry for the uid - skip with a reason in that case; (4) watch bad-actor test should also assert no .troupe/history.sqlite was created. Also: NFR-001 atomicity is proven for encode-time failure only; SQLite mid-write failure relies on eventsourcing's single transaction.

issues.title: show: plain scalars valid in YAML 1.2 core misread by ruamel safe-load (dates, <<, signed hex, 1_000)
issues.description: Found in WP01 review (troupe-config-get-show-01M411XB). yamlout reuses writeback.scalars.choose_style, whose can_plain uses troupe's own YAML 1.2 core resolver (research R-13). Strings like '2001-12-14', '-0x10', '+0x10', '0x1_0', '-0o7', '0b101', '1_000', '-1_0', '=' and the key '<<' render plain. Under YAML 1.2 core they read back as the same strings, but ruamel safe-load (the oracle named in research D-8 / plan Testing) reads dates as datetime.date, signed/underscored numbers as int, '=' raises ConstructorError, and '<<' is treated as a merge key (k '<<: {a: 1}' reads back as {a: 1}; '<<: 29' raises). Decide: (a) amend NFR-001/D-8 to state YAML 1.2 core is the read-back schema and keep fixtures free of these, or (b) make show (and possibly set) quote strings that ruamel/YAML 1.1-style resolvers would re-type. WP03 integration fixtures (e.g. tests/integration/test_show.py uses b: 2001-12-14, c: 1_000) will hit this if parsed back with ruamel safe-load.
issues.close_reason: Fixed by D-10 in WP01 cycle 2 (yamlout quotes strings YAML 1.1/1.2 readers misread; exponent floats keep a '.'); merged to main in a589041

issues.title: yamlcore docstring says no other module imports ruamel; yamlout now does (D-10 probe)
issues.description: WP01 cycle 2 (troupe-config-get-show) added a ruamel safe-load read-back probe in src/troupe/yamlout.py (documented exception there). src/troupe/yamlcore.py module docstring still states 'No other module imports ruamel'. issues.title: show: mapping keys >1024 chars do not read back
issues.description: troupe config show renders keys as implicit keys ('k': v). YAML forbids implicit keys longer than 1024 chars, so a theatre with such a key (loader accepts explicit '? key' syntax) yields show output that does not parse back (NFR-001 gap). Found by WP01 implementer, mission troupe-config-get-show-01M411XB. Contract silent; fix would need explicit-key layout ('? key' / ': value') — PO decision.
